title: Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey on Bank Lending Practices (SLOOS), 14:00 ET — the edition that tells you what kind of edition May-2027 will be
source: EST: derived from federalreserve.gov's published 2027 FOMC calendar (monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm, fetched direct 2026-09-09, HTTP 200 — the January 2027 meeting is 26-27), applied through the release-date rule audited against 67 SLOOS releases 2010-02-01 -> 2026-08-03 during the never-assessed initial research of sloos-2027-05-03, 2026-09-09: the release is the Monday five sessions after the FOMC's final day, shifted to the next business day only when that Monday is a federal holiday or the market is shut (3 exceptions in 67, all named). Wednesday 2027-01-27 + 5 days = Monday 2027-02-01, which is not a federal holiday. Filed estimate because federalreserve.gov publishes no 2027 newsevents page yet (2027-february.htm returned HTTP 404 on 2026-09-09), because the FOMC calendar carries the Fed's own 'tentative until confirmed at the meeting immediately preceding it' caveat, and because this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep
notes: PROPOSED as the leading indicator for sloos-2027-05-03, not as a tradable date — the same relationship treasury-borrowing-estimates-2027-05-03 has with its own 2026-11-02 sibling. Two things make this edition load-bearing for the May one. First, it is the last SLOOS before it, so its C&I standards-and-demand direction is the base the May edition is read against. Second, it is the earliest place to see whether the NONDEPOSITORY FINANCIAL INSTITUTION special questions — carried by both the April-2026 and July-2026 editions, the bank credit that funds private credit — have become a standing series rather than a two-quarter experiment; that question is registered as FT-sloos-2027-05-03-3. Note this release lands in JANUARY-adjacent territory only by luck of the calendar: the Monday-after-FOMC rule has put the winter edition in January four times since 2010 (2011-01-31, 2012-01-30, 2022-01-31, and 2012 aside every other year in February), so the 'January/February' language on federalreserve.gov/data/sloos is a range, not a month. Impact low, matching sloos-2026-11-02 and sloos-2027-05-03, and for the same measured reason: KRE's excess vs SPY across 67 releases is +0.109%, p=0.496. Estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
